findings.text: blocking: test_a_full_server_reranks_signals asserts server_module._rerank_signals is True, which the landed change at imas_codex/llm/server.py:1894 fails (server_mode_gate.log records 1 failed, 2 passed, EXIT=1); the landed change leaves the repository's llm test module red at the merged head and no plan node owns the repair, so the expectation must be flipped to False before this change lands.

follow-on: the module-level comment above _rerank_signals still states on for a full or DD-path server that may spend a judgement, contradicting the unconditional _rerank_signals = False at :1894; the comment-only head commit f244d24d edited nearby tool comments but left this one wrong, so a reader reconstructs the old ship rule from it.

follow-on: the ship-off decision rests on a pool-60 p95 of 5.022 s against a 5 s limit, a 0.022 s margin on one wall-clock measurement on a shared node (the two arms' p95 differ by 0.5 ms, 5.0218 against 5.0223); the rule as written is applied correctly, but the decision is fragile to node load and a re-measurement could invert it.
